change: a signed-in teacher is not an anonymous request on the analysis route, so another class's lock no longer shuts her out of a lab she has open
_context: Reported as "the 1.1 lab will not unlock even when it's unlocked".
The 1.1 lab is not a terminal lab. It is the phishing analysis activity served
by routes/analysis.js, which is why nothing named 1.1 exists in config/labs/.
gateFor() resolved a signed-in teacher as anonymous. student() answers for
students only, so a teacher token returns null, and the route read that null as
"nobody is signed in" and ran the cross-class rule on her. That rule refuses
whenever ANY class anywhere has closed the activity, so a lock set at another
school shut her out of a lab her own class had open. Her own row was never read.
routes/labs.js settled this on 2026-09-09 off the same complaint. This route was
written two days earlier and never got the port.

_superseded: SUPERSEDED IN PART by deploy-gates/2026-09-14-board-277-labs-open.json, later the
same day. This manifest is kept as the record of what shipped in PR #666, and its
three retired checks are listed below rather than deleted, because a manifest that
quietly loses checks reads like it never had them.
Board 277 opened the anonymous case, so three checks here can no longer fail and
the teacher-branch mutation      deleting the branch is now unobservable,
because every caller without a student row
the role-check mutation          same reason; the role still decides the lab
the anonymous-rule mutation      the rule it defended is the one 277 retired
The teacher branch itself is KEPT. It is a permit rather than a guard, so being
redundant makes it harmless, while a mutation claiming to prove something it
cannot is the hollow thing. If the anonymous rule is ever narrowed again, that
branch is what keeps a teacher out of the support queue.
